## Purpose

Find out which known factors shape the metabolite profiles of the cell lines,
in particular culture batch and tissue of origin, and whether they are
confounded with each other.

**Decision supported:** which covariates the differential models need
(planned design so far: `~ tissue + covariates + mutation`).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/01_injections.rds`, `01_lines.rds`
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_github/Cellline_mappings_shorthouse.csv`:
  batch, plate and tissue per injection from the authors' GitHub repository
  (`shorthouse-mrc/CellLine_Metabolomics` @ cce3b15). **Local only** (no licence
  in the repository); this notebook does not run without it.

## Methods

Each injection was assigned its culture batch (7 batches; sub-batches such as
6A/6B were combined) and the tissue label of Shorthouse et al. (11 tissues plus
"Unknown"). Intensities were averaged per line and transformed with
log2 after half-minimum imputation of values <= 0 (see Audit 1). Principal component analysis
was run on the ion-wise standardised values. For each of the first ten
components, the variance explained by tissue and by batch was estimated as the
R² of a one-way linear model (lines grown in a single batch only for batch).
Per ion, association with tissue was tested by one-way ANOVA, and with batch by
ANOVA after adjusting for tissue; p-values were adjusted with the
Benjamini–Hochberg procedure.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(limma)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/transform.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_02_structure_batch_tissue")

injections <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "01_injections.rds"))
lines <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "01_lines.rds"))
mapping_file <- file.path(raw_dir, "shorthouse_github", "Cellline_mappings_shorthouse.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(mapping_file))

Y <- lines$intensities
# log2 after half-minimum imputation of values <= 0 (Audit 1)
A <- log2_half_minimum(Y)
```

## 1. Batch and tissue per line

```{r batch}
mapping <- readr::read_csv(mapping_file, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
    transmute(
        injection_id = as.character(dsIdx),
        batch = sub("[A-Za-z]$", "", sub("_.*$", "", dsPert)),   # Batch6A -> Batch6
        tissue_paper = Tissue
    )
stopifnot(all(injections$injections$injection_id %in% mapping$injection_id))

per_line <- injections$injections %>%
    left_join(mapping, by = "injection_id") %>%
    group_by(line) %>%
    summarise(
        n_batches = n_distinct(batch),
        batch = if (n_distinct(batch) == 1) first(batch) else "several",
        tissue = paste(sort(unique(tissue_paper)), collapse = "; "),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    slice(match(rownames(Y), line))

count(per_line, n_batches)
per_line %>% filter(n_batches > 1) %>% pull(line)
count(per_line, tissue, sort = TRUE)

tile <- count(per_line, tissue, batch)
p <- ggplot(tile, aes(batch, reorder(tissue, n, sum), fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#DEEBF7", high = "#08519C") +
    labs(x = "Culture batch", y = "Tissue (Shorthouse et al.)", fill = "Lines",
         title = "Small tissues sit in one or two batches; lung is spread over all") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "tissue_by_batch", fig_dir, width = 8, height = 5)
p
```

## 2. Principal components

```{r pca}
pca <- prcomp(A, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
var_explained <- summary(pca)$importance[2, 1:10]
scores <- as_tibble(pca$x[, 1:4]) %>% mutate(line = rownames(A)) %>% left_join(per_line, by = "line")

p <- ggplot(tibble(pc = factor(1:10), var = var_explained), aes(pc, var)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
    labs(x = "Principal component", y = "Share of variance", title = "Scree plot (log2, 1096 ions, 175 lines)") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "scree", fig_dir)
p

plot_scores <- function(x, y, colour_by, title) {
    lv <- sort(unique(scores[[colour_by]]))
    ggplot(scores, aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]], colour = .data[[colour_by]])) +
        geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = uc_palette(lv)) +
        labs(title = title, colour = NULL,
             x = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", x, 100 * var_explained[as.integer(sub("PC", "", x))]),
             y = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", y, 100 * var_explained[as.integer(sub("PC", "", y))])) +
        theme_uc()
}
for (pair in list(c("PC1", "PC2"), c("PC2", "PC3"))) {
    for (by in c("tissue", "batch")) {
        p <- plot_scores(pair[1], pair[2], by, sprintf("%s vs %s, coloured by %s", pair[1], pair[2], by))
        save_figure(p, sprintf("pca_%s_%s_%s", pair[1], pair[2], by), fig_dir, width = 7.5, height = 5)
        print(p)
    }
}
```

## 3. Variance explained by tissue and batch

```{r r2}
r2 <- function(score, factor) {
    ok <- !is.na(factor)
    summary(lm(score[ok] ~ factor(factor[ok])))$r.squared
}
batch_single <- ifelse(per_line$n_batches == 1, per_line$batch, NA)
r2_table <- tibble(
    pc = factor(1:10),
    tissue = sapply(1:10, function(k) r2(pca$x[, k], per_line$tissue)),
    batch = sapply(1:10, function(k) r2(pca$x[, k], batch_single))
)
r2_table

p <- r2_table %>%
    pivot_longer(c(tissue, batch), names_to = "factor", values_to = "r2") %>%
    ggplot(aes(pc, r2, fill = factor)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(batch = "#D55E00", tissue = "#009E73")) +
    labs(x = "Principal component", y = expression(R^2), fill = NULL,
         title = "Batch explains more of the leading components than tissue",
         subtitle = sprintf("batch: %d lines grown in one batch; tissue: all %d lines", sum(!is.na(batch_single)), nrow(per_line))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "r2_tissue_batch_by_pc", fig_dir)
p
```

## 4. Ions associated with tissue and with batch

```{r per-ion}
one <- !is.na(batch_single)
p_tissue <- apply(A, 2, function(v) anova(lm(v ~ factor(per_line$tissue)))[1, 5])
p_batch <- apply(A[one, ], 2, function(v) {
    anova(lm(v ~ factor(per_line$tissue[one]) + factor(batch_single[one])))[2, 5]
})
c(ions = ncol(A),
  tissue_bh_0.05 = sum(p.adjust(p_tissue, "BH") < 0.05),
  batch_given_tissue_bh_0.05 = sum(p.adjust(p_batch, "BH") < 0.05))

p <- bind_rows(
    tibble(test = "tissue", p = p_tissue),
    tibble(test = "batch (given tissue)", p = p_batch)
) %>%
    ggplot(aes(p)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, boundary = 0, fill = "#56B4E9") +
    facet_wrap(~ test) +
    labs(x = "ANOVA p-value per ion", y = "Number of ions",
         title = "Batch leaves a stronger per-ion signature than tissue",
         subtitle = "A peak near 0 means many ions are associated") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "per_ion_pvalues", fig_dir, width = 9, height = 4)
p
```

## 5. Does adjusting for batch change a typical comparison?

As an example, KRAS-mutant lung lines are compared with the other lung lines,
with and without batch in the model. Lines grown in several batches are
assigned the batch in which most of their injections were measured. If the
mutation groups are spread evenly over the batches, adjusting for batch should
change little; if not, it protects against batch effects being read as
mutation effects.

```{r batch-example}
# majority batch per line: the batch with the most injections of that line
majority_batch <- injections$injections %>%
    left_join(mapping, by = "injection_id") %>%
    count(line, batch) %>%
    group_by(line) %>%
    slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(line, batch)

# KRAS status from the mutation table; lung from the tissue labels of step 02
cell_lines <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_cell_lines.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
gene_status <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_gene_status.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
kras_lines <- gene_status$line[gene_status$gene == "KRAS" & gene_status$status == "mutation"]
lung <- tibble(line = cell_lines$line[cell_lines$tissue %in% "Lung"]) %>%
    left_join(majority_batch, by = "line") %>%
    mutate(kras = factor(if_else(line %in% kras_lines, "KRAS", "other"), levels = c("other", "KRAS")))

# are KRAS-mutant lines spread evenly over the batches?
table(batch = lung$batch, kras = lung$kras)
fisher.test(table(lung$batch, lung$kras))$p.value

# limma with and without batch, all metabolites at once
fit_kras <- function(design) {
    fit <- eBayes(lmFit(t(A[lung$line, ]), design))
    topTable(fit, coef = "krasKRAS", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
}
without_batch <- fit_kras(model.matrix(~ kras, lung))
with_batch <- fit_kras(model.matrix(~ batch + kras, lung))
c(
    cor_t = cor(without_batch$t, with_batch$t),
    top20_overlap = length(intersect(head(order(without_batch$P.Value), 20), head(order(with_batch$P.Value), 20))),
    p_below_0.01_without = sum(without_batch$P.Value < 0.01),
    p_below_0.01_with = sum(with_batch$P.Value < 0.01)
)

p <- ggplot(tibble(without = without_batch$t, with = with_batch$t), aes(without, with)) +
    geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    labs(x = "t-statistic, ~ kras", y = "t-statistic, ~ batch + kras",
         title = "KRAS vs other lung lines: batch adjustment changes little here",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d lung lines; KRAS spread evenly over batches", nrow(lung))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "kras_with_without_batch", fig_dir)
p
```

## Interpretation and decision

- Culture batch is partly confounded with tissue: several small tissues were
  grown in only one or two batches, whereas lung lines are spread over all
  seven. Seventeen lines (mostly the QC line and repeated lines) occur in
  several batches.
- Batch explains more variance of the leading principal components than tissue,
  and more metabolites are associated with batch (after adjusting for tissue)
  than with tissue. The authors removed metabolites with batch/plate effects,
  but a batch signal remains.
- Within lung, KRAS-mutant lines are spread evenly over the batches, and
  adjusting for batch changes the KRAS comparison little. Batch matters most
  where it is confounded with tissue, i.e. in comparisons across tissues.

**Decision (2026-10-28):** culture batch enters every differential model as one
covariate (`~ batch + tissue + ... + mutation`); lines grown in several batches
are assigned the batch with most of their injections. Adjusting for batch is
the standard approach; removing batch effects beforehand (e.g. ComBat) is not
used, because it can create artificial differences in unbalanced designs.
